question: Does creating a user worker with EdgeRuntime.userWorkers.create report a function that cannot start, so a deploy can refuse it before the live version changes?
runtime: public.ecr.aws/supabase/edge-runtime@sha256:ad45164b7548bf5820ed7be714789c17ac2865edce79a09cfb4c3756c3d365a8 (the pinned v1.77.4), one throwaway container from docs/evidence/functions-sandbox-hardening-2026-10-30/run_main.sh with a spike main service, removed afterwards; not the hardened launch (no read only root, no dropped capabilities), so whether the boot route works under the hardened container is still open
options: memoryLimitMb 150, workerTimeoutMs 20000, forceCreate true, tmpFsConfig quota 64 MiB, the same permissions object as lab/functions/main/index.ts

syntax error.message: worker boot error: failed to bootstrap runtime: failed to create the graph: The module's source code could not be parsed: Unexpected eof at file:///home/deno/functions/v1/syntax/index.ts:2:1

import of a file that does not exist.message: failed to create the graph: Module not found "file:///home/deno/functions/v1/nomodule/missing.ts"

no entry point in the folder.message: failed to bootstrap runtime: could not find an appropriate entrypoint

top level throw (throw new Error at load.note: the error appears only in the container log ('runtime has escaped from the event loop unexpectedly'), so create does not catch it

no Deno.serve call.note: found only at the first request

worker.fetch of the created worker from.result: error 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading streamRid)': a request must be passed on from the original request object; the boot route does not need to send a request

conclusion: A create call catches what a deploy most often gets wrong: a syntax error, a missing or unreadable import, a missing entry point, a type of failure reported before any request. It does not catch a top level throw or a missing Deno.serve; the page must say so and the first call or the log shows those. Time is a few tens of milliseconds for a function whose imports are already cached; an import from the network needs the outbound network and can take seconds, so the boot check needs its own deadline.
